subject: Expansion economics & offset proposal for new workloads
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@optiscale.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expansion pricing question for additional teams

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ramping a second product line (customer insights) and expect an incremental 1.2T tokens / month once it’s in prod.

Primary asks:
- How would that volume map into your per-token volume discounts vs our current committed tier?
- Any ability to offset initial months with credits for the onboarding surge?
- Do you have a simple schedule we can share with procurement for forecasting?

Attaching our Q3 usage snapshot for reference. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

—Jamie
Director, Platform
OptiScale

Attachment: optiscale_usage_report_Q3.csv (text/csv, 85KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@optiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing question for additional teams

Jamie —

Thanks for the snapshot; that helps. Quick summary upfront: we can structure an incremental commit with a blended per-token step that preserves your existing unit economics while giving a short-term onboarding credit to smooth costs during the ramp.

High-level proposal (details attached):
- Incremental committed slab: 1.25T tokens/mo for 12 months as an add-on to your current commit.
- Blended per-token pricing for incremental slab: 18% off list for the first 3 months, then 12% thereafter (applies only to tokens billed against the incremental slab).
- Onboarding offset: one-time credit equal to 10% of the estimated first 3 months of incremental spend (applied as invoice credit).

I’ve attached a modeled schedule and a short pricing summary. If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in contracts to draft a simple amendment. Would you like to schedule a 30-min to walk through the numbers Monday?

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_commit_schedule_v2.xlsx, redwood-pricing-summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Expansion pricing question for additional teams (internal)

Q: Do we want to make the 10% onboarding offset conditional on a minimum ramp? I worry about being overly generous with short-lived spikes.

Suggested tweak: onboarding credit vests over two billing cycles and only applies if usage hits >= 60% of the incremental slab within 45 days. If they miss the threshold, credit is reduced pro-rata. That protects us but keeps the commercial signal.

Also: confirm that blended discount stacks with any existing enterprise credits.

—Ben
Sr. Sales Manager

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Expansion pricing question for additional teams (internal)

Agree with the vesting condition. I’ll propose:
- 10% onboarding credit applied in two equal installments across first two invoices.
- Eligibility: incremental usage >= 60% of committed slab during first 45 days.
- Miss threshold → credit reduced proportionally to actual usage / 60%.

Marissa — can you draft the amendment language and a one-page procurement summary we can send to OptiScale legal? I’ll take the customer call Monday at 10am PT.

Thanks.
Rachel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Expansion pricing question for additional teams (internal)

On it — I’ve put a short procurement summary in the attached spreadsheet and drafted amendment bullets for legal. Two notes for the external facing doc:
- Make the onboarding credit procedural (how it posts to invoice) — procurement teams like that clarity.
- Add an explicit clause that the blended discount only applies to usage billed against the incremental slab and does not retroactively change prior invoices.

Attaching: proposed_commit_schedule_v2.xlsx (updated)

—Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@optiscale.com>, contracts@optiscale.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing question for additional teams

Jamie / OptiScale team —

Thanks for the patience. Quick recap of the agreed commercial approach and next steps:

1) Incremental commit: 1.25T tokens / month added for 12 months (OPT-2026-004 amendment).
2) Pricing: blended per-token discount on incremental slab — 18% off list for months 1–3, 12% off list for months 4–12.
3) Onboarding offset: one-time credit equal to 10% of estimated first 3 months spend, paid as two invoice credits; eligibility requires hitting >=60% of incremental slab within 45 days, otherwise credit reduced pro-rata.
4) No change to your existing committed slab pricing; this only affects the incremental slab.
5) Next step: contracts@optiscale.com — we’ll send a short amendment and a procurement summary (one-page). Expect a DocuSign link once both legal teams sign off.

If that matches your expectation I’ll open the amendment and share the DocuSign URL here. Ready to proceed on our side.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: proposed_commit_schedule_v2.xlsx, redwood-pricing-summary.pdf
